study.title: Brain Connectivity and Topological Reorganization of Multiple Functional Networks in Subjective Cognitive Decline After Acupuncture Intervention: A Secondary Analysis of a Randomized Controlled Trial
study.article_type: Original Research / Secondary Analysis of Randomized Controlled Trial
study.study_design: Secondary analysis of a 12-week randomized, sham acupuncture-controlled trial based on multi-model magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) data
study.randomization: Randomization determined using SAS Version 9.2 software in blocks of six participants by a statistical analyst
study.blinding: Except for the acupuncturists who could not be blinded due to the nature of the intervention, both the patients and the evaluators were blinded to the group allocation. Participants were separated by cubicles to avoid communication.
study.population: Individuals with subjective cognitive decline (SCD) aged 55-75 years recruited from Beijing Shunyi community service centers
study.inclusion_criteria: (a) aged 55-75 years, (b) normal neuropsychological performance adjusting for age and education in tests, including the Mini-Mental State Examination (MMSE), Auditory Verbal Learning Test (AVLT), Trail Making Test (TMT), and Animal Vocabulary Test (AFT) and (c) normal or near normal function in daily life activities. Participants were screened through the Subjective Cognitive Decline Questionnaire 9 (SCD-Q9, score >5).
study.exclusion_criteria: Presence of severe systemic diseases, neurological diseases, MRI contraindications, and abnormal brain structures or white matter hyperintensities. If any patient experienced claustrophobia or discomfort, or actively indicated that they could not complete the subsequent scans, the scanning process was immediately terminated.

arms.dropouts: One participant excluded due to abnormal brain structure, excessive head motion during scanning, or not completing the intervention or the second MRI scan

extraction_notes.note: Supplementary Tables 1-5 and Supplementary Fig. 1 are referenced in the text but not provided in the PDF. These contain: (Table 1) FC results adjusted for age, sex, education, head motion; (Table 2) ANCOVA results for FCs with baseline differences; (Table 3) pre- and post-intervention AUC values for all nine ROIs; (Table 4) topological property results adjusted for covariates; (Table 5) head motion parameters; (Fig. 1) post-hoc power analysis. None of these supplementary data could be extracted.
Adverse events are not explicitly reported or discussed anywhere in the main text. The paper does not include a dedicated adverse events section.
Expectancy and credibility measures are not reported. The paper does not describe any formal expectancy, treatment credibility, or allocation guessing assessment instrument.
Deqi was required as a procedural criterion in the AG but was not formally measured or reported as an outcome variable. No validated deqi scale (e.g., MASS, SASSQQ) was used.

The paper states 72 participants were 'randomly assigned' and 66 completed; however, it states AG had 35 and SG had 31 completers (total = 66). The n_assigned per arm is not explicitly stated as 36+36, but this is implied by '1:1 ratio' from 72 total. The extraction records n_assigned as 36 per arm as an inference from '1:1 ratio' and 72 total.

The paper states this is a 'secondary analysis' of data from a previous RCT (Wang X et al., 2024, ref [6]). The original trial used seed-based FC; this secondary analysis used Dosenbach atlas ROI-based whole-brain FC matrix. Sample sizes and design are drawn from the primary trial.

The paper notes five FCs showed significant group × time interactions, but the directionality description is slightly inconsistent: it says two FCs within SMN were 'increased by acupuncture' and three SMN-CON FCs 'significantly decreased.' The specific assignment of FC_E1 and FC_E2 as within-SMN (increased) and FC_E3, FC_E4, FC_E5 as SMN-CON inter-network (decreased) is inferred from the text description and Fig. 2 legend, since the paper does not provide a single table listing all five FCs with their network assignments and directions together.

Fig. 2B provides bar graphs for mean and SE of FC values pre/post for each group for all five significant FCs, but exact numerical values (beyond direction of change) are not tabulated in the text and cannot be reliably read from the PDF figure.

The neuroimaging thresholds differ between the two analysis types: p < 0.001 for functional connectivity interactions and p < 0.05 for topological properties. Both use the 5000-permutation test. No multiple comparison correction (e.g., FDR, FWE, Bonferroni) is explicitly applied beyond the permutation approach for either analysis.

The paper references a 'posterior insular' ROI in the Fig. 2 caption ('left posterior insular and left parietal lobe') but the corresponding Dosenbach atlas ROI MNI coordinates are not separately listed in Table 1. This FC (FC between left posterior insula and left parietal lobe) appears to be one of the five significant FCs described in text and Fig. 2A/2B. However, no separate MNI coordinates for 'left posterior insular' are provided in Table 1 — possibly subsumed under another listed ROI or an error in the paper.

The assignment of specific FCs to 'within-SMN' vs 'SMN-CON inter-network' is done based on the text description and Fig. 2 legend. The paper states two FCs within SMN increased and three inter-network FCs decreased, but does not provide a summary table mapping each FC pair to its specific network category. The extraction above follows the most plausible reading: left parietal lobe – right parietal lobe and left precentral gyrus – right parietal lobe as within-SMN; left vFC – left thalamus, right precentral gyrus – left PCC, and left middle insular – left PCC as SMN-CON. This is consistent with Dosenbach's network assignments referenced in the paper.

Global signal regression is not reported as applied or not applied in the preprocessing pipeline. This is potentially relevant for interpretation of negative functional connectivity values (e.g., insula-PCC negative connectivity).

The paper reports ANCOVA results for three FCs showing baseline differences (F = 8.227, p = 0.006, Partial η2 = 0.115 for middle insular-PCC specifically), but full ANCOVA results for all three baseline-different FCs are in Supplementary Table 2, which was not available.

The paper reports the ANCOVA result for middle insular-PCC FC specifically: 'F = 8.227, p = 0.006, Partial η2 = 0.115.' It is unclear whether this is specifically for this one FC or representative of all three baseline-different FCs.
